taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Crother (2008) treated it as a subspecies of the Indian python (P. molurus); Nicholson (2025) recognizes P. bivittatus. Animal Diversity Web also uses the subspecies treatment.
fieldMarks: Large reddish-brown blotches outlined in cream or gold over a pale tan, yellowish-brown or grey base
Arrow-shaped marking on top of the head pointing toward the nose
Heavy-bodied; can exceed 5 m, females larger than males
Every life stage larger than any native snake in its Florida range
behavior: Excellent swimmers, often partly or fully submerged; tied to permanent fresh water
Generalist ambush predator of mammals, birds and reptiles
Everglades mating season is December-April, eggs laid May-June; breeding aggregations of several males with one female
habitat: Grasslands, swamps, marshes, rocky foothills, open woodland and river valleys.
range: Native to northeastern India east through southern China and Southeast Asia and the Malay Peninsula. Established in the Florida Everglades (first nest found in 2006). Not native to Canada.

lookalikes.name: Northern African python
lookalikes.howToTell: Less vivid back pattern and black-and-white belly scales; Burmese python belly scales are white.
